notes.summary: A random variable assigns a number to each outcome. JSO asks on expectation and variance, and on the three standard distributions: binomial, Poisson and normal (mean, variance, probabilities and properties).

concepts.title: Expectation and variance
concepts.body:
• E(X) = Σx p(x); E(X²) = Σx² p(x).
  • Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]².
  • E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X).

concepts.title: Binomial and Poisson
concepts.body:
• Binomial B(n, p): P(X = r) = nCr pr qn−r, q = 1 − p. Mean = np, variance = npq. Mean > variance.
  • Poisson (λ): P(X = r) = e−λλr/r!. Mean = variance = λ. Limit of binomial when n is large and p small (λ = np).

concepts.title: Normal distribution
concepts.body:
• Bell-shaped and symmetric; mean = median = mode; β2 = 3.
  • Standardise: Z = (X − μ)/σ, Z ~ N(0, 1).
  • μ ± σ covers 68.27%, μ ± 2σ covers 95.45%, μ ± 3σ covers 99.73%.
  • Useful areas: P(0 < Z < 1) = 0.3413, P(0 < Z < 1.96) = 0.475, P(0 < Z < 2) = 0.4772.

varieties.name: Expectation and variance
varieties.how: Multiply each value by its probability and add; for variance use E(X²) − [E(X)]².

example.q: X takes 0 and 1 with probabilities 0.3 and 0.7. Find Var(X).

varieties.name: Binomial and Poisson
varieties.how: Use mean = np, var = npq (binomial) or mean = var = λ (Poisson); plug into the PMF for exact probabilities.

example.q: X ~ Poisson with P(X = 1) = P(X = 2). Find the mean.

varieties.name: Normal distribution
varieties.how: Convert X to Z, then use the standard area table and symmetry.

steps: Half the area lies below the mean.

tips: In a binomial, variance/mean = q gives p quickly.
The normal curve is symmetric, so P(Z > a) = P(Z < −a).
traps: For a binomial, variance can never exceed the mean.
Var(aX + b) uses a², and the constant b vanishes.
Z uses σ (SD), not σ² (variance), in the denominator.

formulas.name: Binomial
formulas.expr: P(X=r) = ⁿCᵣ pʳ qⁿ⁻ʳ;  mean np, variance npq

formulas.name: Poisson
formulas.expr: P(X=r) = e^(−λ) λʳ / r!;  mean = variance = λ
